problem: Small merchants lacked an affordable branded loyalty app like Starbucks; Dealyze offered a themeable loyalty and referral program at lower cost than rivals.

founders.name: William Baron
founders.background_notes: YC bio: currently in importing, logistics, wholesale distribution and Amazon sales.

founders.name: Mark Salpeter
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him with no bio.

competitors.name: Belly
competitors.what: Mobile loyalty program for small businesses

competitors.name: FiveStars
competitors.what: Mobile loyalty program for small businesses

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile app and tablet apps with a theming engine; standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Positioned on lower price and branded theming, both easy to copy; Belly and FiveStars were already established.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals already served the segment; Dealyze's outcome is not documented in sources found.

market_need_then: The YC launch post says Belly and FiveStars showed demand for small business mobile loyalty, and Dealyze aimed to serve merchants at a lower price. No usage data found.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand coverage found. Spelling with y invites confusion with Dealize and Dealwise, and the 'deal' root suggests coupons more than loyalty.

outcome_analysis: The outcome of Dealyze is not public. It went through YC W15 with a small seed (about $120K per one database), launched against better known loyalty startups Belly and FiveStars, and no later funding or news was found. YC lists it inactive, but CB Insights still showed it alive, so the end date and cause are unknown and no failure factor is assigned.
notes: Round rests on CB Insights ($0.12M seed 2015-03-19); funding.tech.eu gives a conflicting EUR 109,090 dated 2014-09. A March 2015 article said it had no other outside funding. Exit type is unknown because no shutdown report was found though YC says Inactive. Competitors are from the YC launch post and a TechCrunch piece whose date was not visible; both are from the batch period. dealyze.com returned HTTP 503. Seedtable lists extra founder names (Sam Baron, Will Baron) that are unverified and not included.
